summary:
Earth and Space Science in 8th grade covers the dynamic systems that shape our planet and our connection to the broader universe. The curriculum is generally broken down into core units:

1. Earth's Systems and Spheres

• Geosphere (Lithosphere): The solid rock, minerals, and landforms of Earth, driven by the rock cycle (igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks) and plate tectonics.
• Hydrosphere & Cryosphere: All of Earth’s water (oceans, rivers, lakes) and ice (glaciers and ice caps), governed by the water cycle, ocean currents, and weather patterns.
• Atmosphere: The layers of gases surrounding Earth, focusing on air pressure, wind, the greenhouse effect, and how heat and moisture drive weather and climate.
• Biosphere: All living organisms on Earth and how they interact with the physical environment.

2. Plate Tectonics and Earth's History

• Continental Drift & Plate Boundaries: How Earth's crust is divided into tectonic plates that move via convection currents in the mantle.
• Geologic Events: How convergent, divergent, and transform boundaries cause earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, and mountain building.
• Earth's Timeline: Using the rock record, stratigraphy, and fossils to understand relative dating and Earth's deep history.
